## Teaching points

1. Toxic shock syndrome follows nasal surgery and packing, wounds, burns and childbirth as well as tampon use; ask about recent procedures in anyone with fever, rash and shock.
2. CDC staphylococcal TSS definition: fever of at least 38.9 °C, diffuse macular erythroderma, hypotension, involvement of three or more organ systems, and desquamation 1–2 weeks later.
3. Start vancomycin plus clindamycin (to suppress toxin production) with fluids and vasopressors; narrow to an antistaphylococcal beta-lactam once MSSA is confirmed.
4. Blood cultures are usually negative in staphylococcal TSS; look for the organism at the colonized site (wound, nose, vagina).
5. Remove the toxin source where possible (packing, tampons, collections); a few cases, like this one, resolve without removing an implant.
